intro.data: Encode is reversible, and so is Compress. Chain two reversible steps and the whole journey is reversible. Your tray holds Encode, the lossless finisher, and a lossy look-alike that loses detail. Bring Encode and the lossless finisher onto the board and wire them to reach the archive, leaving the lossy one in the tray.
intro.alchemy: Grind is reversible, and so is Mint. Chain two reversible steps and the whole journey is reversible. Your tray holds Grind, the lossless finisher, and a lossy look-alike that loses detail. Bring Grind and the lossless finisher onto the board and wire them to reach the coin, leaving the lossy one in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: Etch is reversible, and so is Seal. Chain two reversible steps and the whole working is reversible. Your tray holds Etch, the lossless finisher, and a lossy look-alike that loses detail. Bring Etch and the lossless finisher onto the board and wire them to reach the ward, leaving the lossy one in the tray.
intro.abstract: f and the right h are isomorphisms; chained, the composite is too. Here values are concrete: f sends 2 ↦ 2▲ (invertible) and the true h sends 2▲ ↦ 2◆ (invertible), so the whole chain can be undone, while the lossy look-alike sends 2▲ ↦ 8 and cannot. Bring f and the true h from the tray and wire them, leaving the lossy one behind.

afterSuccess.data: Two lossless steps make a lossless whole — Encode then Compress can be undone (decompress, then decode), so the start and the archive are the same up to renaming. Flatten would have lost detail and broken reversibility.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Two lossless steps make a lossless whole — the coin can be returned to the bar. Melt would have lost detail.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Two lossless steps make a lossless whole — the ward can be returned to the sigil. Smear would have lost detail.
afterSuccess.abstract: Two isomorphisms compose to an isomorphism; the lossy look-alike does not. A ≅ C.

reveal.summary: Isomorphisms compose: if A ≅ B and B ≅ C then A ≅ C, with inverse f⁻¹ ∘ h⁻¹. A lossy step breaks reversibility.
notation: A ≅ B and B ≅ C ⟹ A ≅ C
reveal.moreFormal: Isomorphism is an equivalence relation on objects; it composes and reverses. Reversibility is exactly losing no information.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: Compose two lossless codecs and you can still round-trip; one lossy step ruins it.
